decisions.title: Delivery objective

options.label: Local usable loop first
options.consequence: The operator receives daily value after M3 while later orchestration phases continue incrementally.

options.label: Complete P5-P7 first
options.consequence: Architectural breadth lands before the currently unusable operator journey, delaying feedback and value.

decisions.rationale: The operator explicitly prioritized a usable local product before further refactor completion.

decisions.title: Browser authorization

options.label: Per-browser Hive OAuth session
options.consequence: Each browser proves the single Hive identity and receives a separate revocable local session without seeing daemon tokens.

options.label: Open trusted-LAN API
options.consequence: Any LAN client can read configuration and invoke execution controls without browser authorization.

options.label: Local account or password
options.consequence: A second identity store and credential lifecycle must be operated alongside Hive.

decisions.rationale: Hive remains the only identity provider while browser authorization becomes explicit.

decisions.title: Browser-session lifetime

options.label: Persistent session without routine server expiry
options.consequence: A five-year cookie survives idle and browser restart until logout, Hive disconnect, or owner change.

options.label: Short inactivity or absolute expiry
options.consequence: The operator must repeatedly reauthenticate and local work depends on session-renewal timing.

decisions.rationale: The first release favors generous persistence and explicit invalidation.

decisions.title: WAI artifact shape

options.label: Umbrella roadmap plus child workstreams
options.consequence: Each milestone has one canonical spec, bounded decomposition, and an independent outcome gate.

options.label: One M0-M7 implementation plan
options.consequence: The plan becomes too broad for reliable decomposition and can conceal unfinished milestone outcomes.

decisions.rationale: The release train needs independently shippable, reviewable milestones.

decisions.title: Execution identity ownership

options.label: Permanent generation model in M2
options.consequence: M3-M5 use the same identity that M6 later claims and resumes.

options.label: Temporary first-release identity then M6 redesign
options.consequence: Crash continuation requires replacing lifecycle state after executors already depend on it.

decisions.rationale: The first usable release must not create lifecycle follow-up debt.

decisions.title: Attached OpenCode launch handshake

options.label: Pre-create and persist remote session before prompt
options.consequence: Every possibly active remote writer has a durable abort identity across crashes.

options.label: Discover session ID from running-client output
options.consequence: A crash after remote work starts but before output persistence can leave an unknown orphan writer.

decisions.rationale: OpenCode exposes create, prompt, and abort session operations, enabling a two-stage durable handshake.

decisions.title: OpenCode compatibility

options.label: Explicit certified versions
options.consequence: The audited 1.18.19 contract launches; other versions are blocked until fixtures and a golden path certify them.

options.label: Assume all installed versions work
options.consequence: CLI, API, or event drift can silently corrupt execution behavior.

decisions.rationale: OpenCode evolves quickly and current event drift is already confirmed.

decisions.title: Restart behavior before M6

options.label: Safe interruption without automatic continuation
options.consequence: Accidental restart retains history, fences writers, and requires explicit retry.

options.label: Ship existing automatic resume
options.consequence: Known ownership and persistence windows can produce duplicate writers or lost resumed output.

decisions.rationale: The operator accepts finish-before-planned-restart, but accidental restart must fail safely.

decisions.title: Attached-server credentials

options.label: Environment-variable name only
options.consequence: Profiles persist only the variable name and secrets stay out of JSON, argv, logs, and responses.

options.label: Profile or command-line password
options.consequence: Long-lived credentials can appear in persistent configuration or process inspection.

decisions.rationale: The attached-server adapter needs authentication without expanding secret exposure.

decisions.title: Trusted-LAN transport controls

options.label: Do not enforce TLS, Secure cookie, CORS, or Origin policy
options.consequence: Existing plain-HTTP LAN operation remains supported and documentation carries the plaintext-session risk.

options.label: Require transport or origin controls
options.consequence: First use depends on new certificate, proxy, or browser-origin deployment work.

decisions.rationale: The operator explicitly accepted trusted-LAN plaintext operation for this release.

decisions.title: Executor certification order

options.label: Attached OpenCode, direct OpenCode, Claude
options.consequence: The operator's existing OpenCode server becomes useful first; shared behavior then certifies the other adapters.

options.label: Certify all executors together
options.consequence: The first usable release waits for independent adapter defects to be resolved together.

decisions.rationale: The operator supplied this priority order.

obstacles.obstacle: The current OAuth handoff authenticates only the daemon, and transient Hive failures can be confused with explicit disconnect.
obstacles.countermeasure: Create browser-bound one-time handoffs, hashed local sessions tied to the stable owner subject, and separate explicit disconnect from connectivity loss.

obstacles.obstacle: The attached client can start work in the server default directory and reveal its remote session ID only after work begins.
obstacles.countermeasure: Pre-create the remote session for the canonical worktree, persist its ID, then prompt that known session with dynamic directory enforcement.

obstacles.obstacle: MsgStore subscription and final log migration have confirmed races that can omit live or trailing output.
obstacles.countermeasure: Make snapshot-plus-subscribe atomic, acknowledge batch completion, await raw and normalized persistence, and use resumable idempotent migration.

obstacles.obstacle: Stopping the local attached client does not prove the independent remote OpenCode session stopped.
obstacles.countermeasure: Abort by durable remote session ID and verify both local process-group and remote-session quiescence before reporting success.

obstacles.obstacle: Current retry hides history and clears the draft before replacement launch succeeds.
obstacles.countermeasure: Delay supersession and draft deletion until replacement startup commits; retain both on failure.

obstacles.obstacle: Background startup recovery can race mutations and resume with incomplete logging or stale ownership.
obstacles.countermeasure: Add a recovery readiness barrier, fence known generations, disable pre-M6 auto-resume, and expose interrupted state with explicit retry.

obstacles.obstacle: M2, adapter launch, and M6 can each invent a different ownership or generation model.
obstacles.countermeasure: Define the durable generation schema in M2 and require every later adapter and recovery claim to use it unchanged.

obstacles.obstacle: A broad umbrella can be marked complete while child runtime evidence or review findings remain open.
obstacles.countermeasure: Use one WAI child spec per milestone and forbid closure until deterministic tests, live evidence, review, and remediation pass on the same state.

assumptions.claim: The local OpenCode executable is version 1.18.19, the first certified compatibility baseline.
OpenCode exposes session creation with directory context, prompting an existing session, and session abort.
assumptions.probe: Context7 /anomalyco/opencode documentation query on 2026-08-21 returned session.create, session.prompt, directory, and POST /session/{id}/abort contracts.

assumptions.claim: The current node OAuth callback consumes a handoff once and stores Hive access/refresh credentials only in node-side credential storage.
assumptions.probe: Read crates/server/src/routes/oauth.rs:98-137 and confirmed take_oauth_handoff followed by node-side save_credentials.

assumptions.claim: The umbrella workstream tracker and canonical roadmap file exist before spec promotion.
A real Hive deployment, non-loopback browser, and authenticated OpenCode 1.18.19 server can be made available for the first-release live acceptance run.
assumptions.probe: Run the M3 real-LAN acceptance procedure against the final release commit.

questions.asked: Should the next tranche optimize for the complete orchestration refactor or for a usable local product loop first?
Should the trusted-LAN node API remain open or require each browser to complete Hive OAuth?
Should the first release use generous/no routine browser-session timeouts?
Should this roadmap pass through /wai:prd-new before detailed implementation planning?
Must automatic in-flight crash continuation block first use, or may planned restarts require active work to finish?
Should the first release enforce TLS, CORS, Origin policy, or other transport controls?
Which executor paths should be certified first?

no_decision_points_reason: All material product and sequencing forks are settled. Missing dependencies, failed gates, unavailable review panels, or implementation defects require remediation or explicit operator escalation; none is an anticipated halt that this umbrella should authorize automatically.
